_comment: The hand-written half. Edit this daily; fetch-data.mjs merges it with FRED and never overwrites it.
summary: Treasury yields fell across every maturity today and credit is still getting more expensive. The 10 year is at 5.07% and the 30 year at 5.41%, both down about 7 basis points. Meanwhile high yield spreads closed yesterday at *343 basis points*, the widest since the 5th of November. What does this even mean? A spread is the extra yield a company pays over the government for the same maturity. Since the 12th the 10 year has gone essentially nowhere and that spread has widened 23 basis points, so the all-in cost for a high yield borrower went from 8.16% to 8.31% without any help from rates. Credit is repricing on its own. Here is the part worth noticing. The widening is not where fear usually shows up. Investment grade moved 3 basis points. CCC, the worst paper in the market, moved 15 on a spread of over 1,300, which is noise. The high yield index moved 23 on a spread of 320, which is not. The pain is in the liquid middle, the paper everyone owns. That is not a default story, that is a selling story. Funds raising cash sell what has a bid, not what has a problem. Mixing this all in a pot: oil is down 16% on the month, the Fed hikes in December, and credit is tightening the screws without the Treasury market's permission.
_fedPath_note: Every FOMC decision since the last hike, oldest first: the date, the upper bound of the target range after it, and hike / cut / hold. Drawn as the staircase under the Fed and listed in its card. Add a row after each meeting.

news.what: High yield spreads widened to 343 basis points, the widest since 5 November, after touching 320 on the 12th. The high yield effective yield is 8.31%.
Treasury yields fell across the curve. The 10 year is at 5.07% and the 30 year at 5.41%, both down roughly 7 basis points.
Investment grade widened 3 basis points over the same stretch against 23 for high yield. The move sits in the liquid middle of the market, not in CCC.
Crude fell below $83, down 16% on the month. Brent is $91.50.
Market now fully prices a 25bp hike in December, and more next year. Core inflation rising faster than expected says the oil shock has seeped into core services.
Treasuries did not catch a bid during the AI selloff. Funds are liquidating bonds to raise cash as AI infrastructure stocks unwind.
Continuing jobless claims tested their lowest level in over three years.
October CPI: headline +0.4% MoM and core +0.3%, both above expectations. No year over year rate published, last year's shutdown left no base month.

_oil_note: Optional daily override. Set asOf to the date you read them and fill wti/brent. Used only while newer than FRED's print - if you stop updating, it falls back to FRED automatically rather than showing an ever-staler number.
_curve_note: Optional hand entry for a yield FRED has not published yet. Same rule as oil: only used while newer than FRED. notes/alert are display only. Put alert on whatever the day's story is: it turns the figure rust and is the only thing telling a first-time visitor where to look. strain is the quieter version: a smaller crack on the summit, number stays in ink. track is [open, low, now] for one tenor's day, drawn as a path under the summit; use it only when the path matters more than the close, and leave it out otherwise.
